papers.title: Memory and executive functioning show differential associations with scam susceptibility in middle to older adulthood
papers.abstract: Objectives: The rising prevalence of financial exploitation among older adults has prompted research on the cognitive mechanisms underlying financial decision making in later life. Prior work has demonstrated a link between cognitive impairment and financial vulnerability. The present study examined the unique contributions of composite measures of memory and executive functioning to scam susceptibility in middle-aged to older adults without dementia. Methods: One hundred and fifty-one participants (age= 68.2 {+/-} 8.0 years, 72.2% female, years of education= 16.4 {+/-} 2.2) completed standard neuropsychological measures from the Uniform Data Set (UDS), Version 3, and the California Verbal Learning Test, Second Edition, and a self-report scam susceptibility measure. Psychometrically robust composite scores, the UDS-M+ and UDS3-EF, were computed to represent memory and executive functioning domains. Linear regression models examined independent associations between UDS-M+ and UDS3-EF performance and scam susceptibility. Nested model comparisons evaluated unique contributions of the UDS-M+ and UDS3-EF when included in a joint model. Results: Lower UDS-M+ (b= -0.25, 95% CI [-0.45, -0.04], p= .018) and lower UDS3-EF (b= -0.33, 95% CI [-0.54, -0.12], p= .002) scores were independently associated with greater scam susceptibility after adjusting for age, sex, years of education, and income. However, only UDS3-EF remained significant in a joint model. Post hoc analyses revealed that only memory was associated with scam susceptibility in middle-aged adults whereas only executive functioning was significant in older adults. Conclusions: These findings highlight the importance of monitoring memory and executive functioning across middle to older adulthood when considering susceptibility to scams.

papers.title: Parent and Adolescent Agreement on Ratings of ADHD Symptoms
papers.abstract: Objective: Parent-adolescent disagreement in ratings of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms can complicate clinical assessment. This study examined parent - adolescent agreement in ADHD symptom ratings and characteristics associated with disagreement. Method: Participants were 1,008 parent-adolescent dyads recruited from a nationally stratified U.S. community sample. Adolescents were 12--18 years old (49.6% female) and along with their parents completed measures of ADHD and depressive symptoms. Agreement on Inattention (IN), Hyperactivity/Impulsivity (HI), and Total ADHD scores was examined. Item-level agreement was assessed using weighted kappa, Gwet 's AC2, percent agreement, and polychoric correlations. Associations between age, sex, and severity of ADHD and depression with levels of agreement were analyzed. Results: Agreement for ADHD factor and total symptom scores was moderate (intraclass correlations = 0.67--0.71), with moderate-to-strong rank-order correspondence. Adolescents reported slightly higher ADHD symptom levels than parents, although the mean difference was small. Item-level agreement was moderate to high (Gwet 's AC2 = 0.79--0.95). Several HI items demonstrated the kappa's paradox, with relatively low kappa values despite high Gwet's AC2 and percent agreement. Q-correlations revealed low agreement on relative strengths and weaknesses. Age and sex were not associated with disagreement and parent-reported ADHD severity and adolescent-reported depressive symptoms were associated with disagreement. Conclusions: Parent and adolescent ratings showed moderate agreement across boys and girls ages 12-- 18; however, disagreement related to relative strengths and weaknesses. Disagreement was associated with ADHD and depressive symptom severity. Findings suggest that ratings from parents and adolescents offer unique perspectives on the assessment of ADHD symptoms.

papers.title: Late-pregnancy immune and kynurenine signatures predict postpartum depression and brain morphology
papers.abstract: Background: Pregnancy involves profound immune adaptations that may contribute to the development of postpartum depression (PPD); however, the relevant biomarkers and critical time window remain unclear. Therefore, we investigated whether third-trimester and postpartum cytokines and kynurenine pathway (KP) metabolites predict PPD and whether these biological signatures are related to postpartum brain morphology. Methods: Circulating cytokines and KP metabolites were assessed in 140 pregnant women during the third trimester and postpartum. Partial least squares (PLS) regression models were used to identify multivariate biological profiles predictive of PPD, followed by classification and regression tree (CART) analyses to evaluate predictive performance. In a neuroimaging subsample (n=61), voxel-based morphometry examined associations among PPD status, significant PLS-derived components, selected individual biomarkers, and postpartum grey matter volume. Results: A third-trimester cytokine signature including 21 cytokines significantly predicted PPD with high specificity. A third-trimester KP profile, driven primarily by the kynurenic acid/quinolinic acid ratio, also predicted PPD, and the combination of cytokine and KP components improved overall predictive performance to 93.3%. Postpartum biomarkers showed substantially weaker associations with PPD. The cytokine component was differentially associated with postpartum grey matter volume according to PPD status, with opposite associations observed in occipital regions between women who did and did not develop PPD. KP measures also showed distinct associations within sensorimotor regions based on PPD status Conclusions: Late pregnancy immune-inflammatory alterations are associated with subsequent PPD and postpartum brain morphology, supporting the potential utility of pregnancy-derived biological signatures for identifying women at increased risk for PPD.

papers.title: Protocol for a feasibility trial of a co-produced intervention: Enabling Service Users with Severe Mental Illness to Learn about and Engage with Good Oral Health (SMILE)
papers.abstract: Background: People with severe mental illness (SMI) report poorer oral health outcomes than the general population, are less likely to attend regular dental check-ups, and may require additional support to visit a dentist. Our previous research showed that interventions tailored to their needs and support from the mental health care system are needed to improve oral health outcomes in people with SMI. Although there is some provision of urgent dental care for people with SMI, there are currently limited available interventions that integrate dental and mental health care and provide dental support in a mental healthcare setting. To address this gap, the aims of the SMILE project are to 1) co-develop and 2) test the feasibility and acceptability of an oral health intervention for people with SMI, delivered by mental health professionals in secondary community mental health care settings. This paper describes the protocol for the feasibility and acceptability testing of the SMILE intervention. Methods: This is a single-arm, non-randomised feasibility trial assessing the feasibility and acceptability of an intervention to support the oral health of mental healthcare service users with SMI. The intervention was co-produced with service users, carers, mental health and dental health professionals, and includes advice on maintaining good oral hygiene and lifestyle habits to maintain good oral health. The main aim of the study is to assess the feasibility and acceptability of delivering the intervention, using quantitative data collected at baseline, three and six-month follow-up, and qualitative interviews with participants and mental health staff involved in delivering the intervention. Results: The study results will determine whether the intervention can be successfully delivered in secondary community mental health care settings and inform the most appropriate primary and secondary outcomes for a future trial. Conclusion: The findings of this study will inform the feasibility of progression to the pilot stage of a randomised controlled trial to assess the clinical and cost effectiveness of delivering an oral health intervention in a mental healthcare setting.

papers.title: Self-perceived cognition and psychological well-being in patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing maintenance haemodialysis
papers.abstract: Cognitive and psychological difficulties are frequently reported by patients undergoing haemodialysis, yet these experiences are rarely explored within routine clinical assessments. The aim of this study was to examine self-perceived cognition and psychological well-being as patient-reported outcomes in adults with chronic kidney disease undergoing maintenance haemodialysis, and to explore the relationships between these outcomes and sociodemographic, clinical, and biochemical variables. Adults receiving maintenance haemodialysis were recruited from a hospital-based dialysis unit as part of the GoodRENal project, which focuses on developing educational approaches for people on haemodialysis. Participants completed self-report measures assessing perceived cognitive functioning and psychological well-being. Sociodemographic, clinical, and biochemical data routinely collected in dialysis care were obtained from medical records. Associations were examined between self-perceived cognition, psychological well-being, and the available data. Seventy-eight patients took part in the study. Perceived cognitive difficulties were more closely related to indicators of kidney disease severity and metabolic imbalance, whereas psychological well-being showed stronger associations with social and emotional factors. The patients' subjective experiences could not be fully explained by objective clinical indicators alone, suggesting a gap between physiological measures and patient-reported outcomes. Self-perceived cognition and psychological well-being provide clinically relevant information that could complement routine clinical indicators in haemodialysis care.

papers.title: An adaptive technical and behavioral approach for biomarker acquisition in autism with intellectual disability
papers.abstract: Autistic individuals with intellectual disability (ASD+ID) and profound autism are rarely studied in neuroscience research due to barriers including communication challenges, sensory sensitivities, anxiety, and elevated behavioral support needs. Consequently, biomarker development in autism fails to include the portion of the autistic population with highest support needs and greatest potential to benefit from treatments derived from imminent advances in personalized medicine. Here we present a multimodal, participant-centered protocol for simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and eye-tracking (ET) acquisition to advance clinical trial readiness research in this underserved population. The protocol combines individualized behavioral supports and an adaptive EEG-ET acquisition platform. Pre-visit caregiver interviews informed participant-specific research plans, including customized visual supports, reinforcement strategies, and EEG net desensitization procedures. A gaze-contingent stimulus presentation system used participant-preferred videos to support attention to experimental stimuli and behavior consistent with data acquisition (e.g., refraining from movement) while dynamically adapting stimulus delivery based on visual engagement with the assay and real-time assessment of data quality. By quantifying attended trials in real time and prioritizing unattended stimulus classes, the paradigm maximizes acquisition efficiency to minimize participant burden. This approach was utilized to deploy candidate biomarkers with demonstrated replicability in the Autism Biomarkers Consortium for Clinical Trials (ABC-CT): the N170 event-related potential to faces, resting-state EEG, and visual attention to human faces (measured with ET). Feasibility was evaluated in 76 children with ASD+ID (M age = 8.76 years; IQ = 32.4) and a small comparison sample of 8 children with intellectual disability without autism (M age = 8.91 years; IQ = 45.9). Usable EEG data (>7 minutes) were acquired in 61% (ASD+ID) and 88% (ID) of participants, respectively. Sufficient ET data were obtained from 67% (ASD+ID) and 63% (ID) of participants, respectively. Findings demonstrate the feasibility of inclusive biomarker acquisition and provide a framework for expanding participation of individuals with ASD+ID and profound autism in neuroscience research. Ongoing research seeks to evaluate this approach in larger samples and to demonstrate feasibility in multisite research studies.

papers.title: Nucleus Accumbens-Anterior Limb of Internal Capsule Deep Brain Stimulation for Treatment-Resistant Schizophrenia: An Open-label Pilot Study
papers.abstract: We conducted an open-label pilot study of bilateral nucleus accumbens-anterior limb of the internal capsule (NAc-ALIC) deep brain stimulation (DBS) in three patients with treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS). Clinical symptoms, global functioning, cognition, stimulation parameters and intracranial local field potential (LFP) were assessed over 24 weeks. Two patients met the prespecified clinical response criterion, defined as a [≥]40% reduction in Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) total score, by week 8 and showed PANSS reductions of 69.0% and 69.4%, respectively, at week 24. The third patient showed a 18.7% reduction at week 24. Responders showed improvements in global functioning and selected cognitive domains. Longitudinal LFP recordings revealed increased gamma-band relative power and reduced theta-band activity in responders, whereas these changes were less consistent in the non-responder. DBS was generally well tolerated, with transient stimulation-related adverse effects resolving after reprogramming. These findings provide preliminary clinical evidence supporting further investigation of NAc-ALIC DBS in TRS and suggest that individualized programming and intracranial physiological measures may contribute to the identification of treatment-response signatures.

papers.title: Escaping the Negative Attentional Bias in Depression with Real-Time Neurofeedback
papers.abstract: Individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD) show an attentional bias toward negatively valenced stimuli and thoughts. In this study, we applied a closed-loop neurofeedback procedure designed to reduce this bias. Participants were shown composite negative faces and neutral scenes with variable opacity and were instructed to attend to the neutral scene while ignoring the negative face. Internal attentional states were decoded in real time from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data. When a participant's decoded attentional state indicated a failure to ignore the negative faces, the faces became more visible (higher opacity), thus externalizing the brain's attentional lapse in that moment. Forty-eight individuals with MDD were randomly assigned to a real neurofeedback training group (N = 24) or a sham control group (N = 24); the control group received feedback yoked to a participant in the real group. All participants completed three fMRI neurofeedback sessions. The main outcome quantified the extent to which participants got ``stuck'' in the most negative attentional state of focusing strongly on the negative faces. We hypothesized that the real neurofeedback group would learn to escape that state by the end of training, relative to the sham control group. Consistent with our hypothesis, neurofeedback training reduced the probability of getting stuck in the most negative attentional state. In offline analyses, training reduced fMRI activity in the precuneus/posterior cingulate and the medial prefrontal cortex when participants successfully attended to scenes and ignored faces. These results demonstrate the efficacy of remediating the negative attentional bias in depression with closed-loop neurofeedback from real-time fMRI.

papers.title: Does chronotype influence the odds of diabetes comorbidity in bipolar disorder? A cross-sectional analysis of the Our Future Health cohort.
papers.abstract: Background Diabetes is common in people with bipolar disorder, particularly men. Both type 2 diabetes and bipolar disorder are associated with evening chronotype, and men of working-age have later chronotypes than women. However, it is not known whether elevated rates of diabetes in bipolar are explained by evening chronotype, nor whether sex differences in chronotype contribute to higher rates of diabetes observed in men with bipolar disorder. Aim To determine whether evening chronotype increases the likelihood of comorbid type 2 diabetes in bipolar disorder, relative to those with no mental health problems. Additionally, to determine whether any effect differs between men and women. Methods Using data from the Our Future Health cohort, we estimated odds ratios for type 2 diabetes by bipolar disorder diagnosis, chronotype, and their interaction, adjusting for relevant covariates. Results A total of 1,136,694 participants (N = 6,846 with bipolar disorder) were included in the adjusted models. Type 2 diabetes was independently associated with bipolar disorder and evening chronotype. There were no significant differences in the interaction effects of chronotype on the odds of type 2 diabetes in bipolar across the whole sample or when stratified by sex. Conclusions The high prevalence of type 2 diabetes in people (and in men, specifically) with bipolar disorder may be independent of evening chronotype.

papers.title: Multimodal macroscopic brain abnormalities in schizophrenia converge on insular, mediofrontal, and sensorimotor cortices and link with glial cell expression but not with recent evolutionary change
papers.abstract: Background: Schizophrenia is characterized by widespread structural and functional brain abnormalities, yet it remains unclear whether these alterations converge across imaging modalities and whether such convergence is associated with underlying cellular distribution and evolution of the human cortex. Methods: We performed coordinate-based meta-analyses of seven whole-brain neuroimaging modalities, including cortical thickness, gyrification, voxel-based morphometry, amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations, regional homogeneity, regional cerebral blood flow (all based on magnetic resonance imaging), and glucose metabolism based on [18F]-Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography. The analyses included 200 studies (209 datasets) comprising 11,794 patients with schizophrenia and 10,342 healthy controls. After single-modality meta-analyses using seed-based d-mapping, the meta-analytic result maps were integrated using orthonormal projective non-negative matrix factorization. Finally, the resulting component maps were related to maps of cortical cell type-specific gene expression and human-specific cortical evolution. Results: Multimodal integration identified a robust convergence pattern centered in bilateral insular, mediofrontal, and lateral sensorimotor cortices, with the strongest contributions from regional homogeneity, cerebral blood flow, and amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations. The convergence pattern showed significant spatial correspondence with cortical gene expression profiles of astrocytes, microglia, and oligodendrocyte progenitor cells. In contrast, we found no evidence for a preferential localization to regions of human-specific cortical expansion or connectivity. Conclusions: Structural and functional brain abnormalities in schizophrenia converge on an insular-mediofrontal-sensorimotor pattern that aligns with glial gene expression profiles. These results support glia-related regional vulnerability as an organizing principle of multimodal brain abnormalities in schizophrenia.

papers.title: Three Cerebellar Imaging Subtypes in Schizophrenia with Distinct Spatiotemporal Trajectories and Biological Characteristics
papers.abstract: The potential role of the cerebellum in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia (SCZ) has received relatively insufficient attention. Prior studies characterized cerebellar abnormalities mainly at the group level, without fully considering the heterogeneity of the disease. Here, we applied a machine learning approach (Subtype and Stage Inference, SuStaIn) to cross-sectional 3D volumetric MRIs of the cerebellum, including 1,588 individuals with SCZ (638 females; mean age: 31.9 +/- 12.0 years) and 2,341 healthy controls (HC) (1,041 females; mean age: 33.3 +/- 13.6 years), from 17 sites worldwide. SuStaIn identified three distinct spatiotemporal trajectories in cerebellar gray matter volume (GMV) reduction, respectively originating in lobule X (subtype 1), lobule III (subtype 2) and lobule VIIb (subtype 3), with subtypes 1 and 3 corresponding to the posterior lobe and subtype 2 to the anterior lobe. These cross-sectionally inferred trajectories were replicated in two independent samples of 1,334 and 530 patients, respectively. Multimodal analyses using neuroimaging, transcriptomic and behavioral data revealed subtype-specific biological characteristics in brain morphological patterns, cerebellar-cortical connectivity, gene expression and clinical symptoms. Specifically, subtype-related genes were enriched in metabolism-related processes and immunity-related processes, respectively, in subtype 1 and subtype 2; subtype 3 showed more severe brain abnormalities and worse cognitive symptoms. Treatment data from 381 patients, with up to 12 months of follow-up, revealed poorer response to antipsychotic medications (APM) in subtype 2 and subtype 3, but better response to transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in subtype 1, which also had worse emotion-related symptoms. Together, our findings offer a comprehensive characterization of the heterogeneity of cerebellar pathophysiological progresses in SCZ, which may help in developing future clinical stratification and targeted intervention strategies.

papers.title: Patterns of substance use during pregnancy are differentially associated with maternal mental health across the perinatal period
papers.abstract: Background: Substance use during pregnancy can substantially increase risk for postpartum depression and anxiety symptoms, which can have lasting effects on family functioning and child development. However, substance use is often conceptualized as a binary exposure, limiting our understanding of whether specific patterns of use are associated with maternal mental health in the perinatal period. Here, we examined longitudinal patterns of prenatal alcohol use and smoking in relation to maternal depressive and anxiety symptoms across pregnancy and the first two years postpartum. Methods: We analyzed prospective data from the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), a population-based cohort from the UK. Alcohol and cigarette use were assessed across all three trimesters and modeled as longitudinal patterns (abstained, persistent, intermittent, discontinued). Maternal depressive and anxiety symptoms were measured from the second trimester through 21 months postpartum using the Crown-Crisp Experiential Index. Results: Persistent alcohol use was associated with higher depressive and anxiety symptoms and slower symptom declines over time, while women with intermittent or discontinued use had symptom profiles similar to abstainers. By contrast, persistent, intermittent, and quitting smoking patterns were associated with higher symptom levels overall, with persistent smoking additionally associated with steeper declines in symptoms over time. Conclusion: Our findings highlight the importance of considering the persistence and cessation of substance use during pregnancy in the context of maternal mental health, pointing to patterns of persistent substance use as a potential target to inform screening and early intervention for women at higher risk for perinatal psychological distress.

papers.title: Latent Genetic Factors and Causal Pathways Linking Substance Use to Psychiatric and Personality Phenotypes: a Genomic SEM and Mendelian Randomization Study
papers.abstract: Substance use and psychiatric disorders frequently co-occur, but establishing causality of their relationships is difficult given the multifactorial nature of these traits. To assess these relationships, we applied two genetically informed methods using the largest available European-ancestry genome-wide association studies of six substance use behaviors and twelve psychiatric and personality phenotypes. Using Genomic Structural Equation Modelling, we modelled the latent genetic architecture of the psychiatric and personality traits and examined these factors' correlations with substance use traits. A structure with three factors fit the data best: F1 (PTSD, MDD, GAD, ADHD, agreeableness), F2 (BD, SCZ, OCD, openness), and F3 (OCD, GAD, extraversion, neuroticism), which showed differential correlations with substance use. Smoking correlated significantly which each factor, however, strongest with F1, alcohol use showed weak but significant correlations with F1 and F2, and cannabis use showed moderate correlations with F1 and F2, but strongest with F2. Using Mendelian Randomization, we examined bidirectional causal relationships. We found strong evidence that smoking continuation was causally associated with increased bipolar disorder risk, cigarettes per day with increased schizophrenia, and smoking initiation with increased extraversion and decreased agreeableness. Genetic liability to schizophrenia and PTSD were causally associated with increased risk of cannabis use, and schizophrenia with increased alcohol use. Liability to neuroticism, openness and agreeableness was causally linked to smoking behaviors, and extraversion to cannabis use. Most remaining associations showed weak causal evidence, largely due to heterogeneity and pleiotropy. Together, these findings provide evidence for both shared genetic liability and, for a subset of relationships, direct causal effects between substance use behaviors, psychiatric disorders, and personality traits, which can help inform future intervention and prevention research.

papers.title: An Open-Label Multidose Psilocybin Intervention for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
papers.abstract: Importance: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) has a 2% global prevalence, but only about 50% of patients respond to conventional treatment, underscoring the need for additional effective interventions. Objective: To assess the feasibility, safety, and preliminary evidence for efficacy of repeated psilocybin administration in OCD patients who had previously attempted psychotherapy or pharmacotherapy. Design: Waitlist-controlled open label randomized clinical trial. Setting: Data were collected at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine. Participants: Data were analyzed from 30 participants (total randomized N=37, by age, sex and OCD severity) with a failed previous attempt at either pharmacotherapy or evidence-based psychotherapies such as exposure response prevention (ERP). Intervention: Participants received two psilocybin doses over two weeks (20 mg followed by 30 mg, if well-tolerated) under supportive conditions. The immediate-treatment arm received the drug within a month following enrollment, and the waitlist-control arm received identical support and dosing after an 8-week waiting period. Main Outcomes: Clinician-administered Y-BOCS scores was collected one week post each drug administration and one month post session 2. Self-assessed reports were collected for acute subjective effects (Mystical Experience Questionnaire (MEQ), Challenging Experience Questionnaire (CEQ), and 11-Dimensional Altered States of Consciousness (11D-ASC)), State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI), Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II), and Quality of Life Enjoyment and Satisfaction Questionnaire (Q-LES-Q). Results: A total of 37 participants were enrolled in the study (age[SD] years:38.4[11.6] years; 21 [56.75%] female), with 30 [81.08%] completing the 1-month follow-up. We show that two successive doses of psilocybin over two weeks were well-tolerated, leading to improvements in OCD symptoms. Compared with the waitlist group (N=14), the immediate-treatment group (N=16) showed a greater reduction in the Y-BOCS scores (F(2,56)=16.17, p<0.001). After crossover, this improvement persisted one month after the second psilocybin dose for both groups (F(3,84)=29.91, p<0.001). Reductions in Y-BOCS score post sessions were correlated with several acute subjective effects measures, including total scores on MEQ, and individual factors on CEQ and 11D-ASC. Conclusions and Relevance: Repeated psilocybin administration is tolerable and potentially efficacious in reducing OCD symptoms. These results support further investigation of multidose psilocybin protocols as a viable therapeutic approach. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier NCT05546658

papers.title: Drivers of the decline in adolescent life satisfaction over 16 years: Evidence from UK representative household panel data (2009-2024)
papers.abstract: Background: The decline of mental health among adolescents in the UK over the past two decades has occurred amidst many societal and technological changes making it difficult to identify drivers of these trends. We aimed to identify which aspect of life showed the most rapid deterioration in satisfaction in the UK since 2009 and which aspects have become increasingly correlated with mental health. Methods: Between 2009 and 2024, 15,829 adolescents aged 10-15 rated their satisfaction with life as well as five aspects of life (family, friends, school, schoolwork, appearance), via the UK Household Longitudinal Study. Population-weighted regressions were used to estimate annual summary statistics on these items (means, proportions) and the relative associations between satisfaction items and socioemotional difficulties, as measured by the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). Meta-regressions estimated linear changes over time, with interactions testing for heterogeneity across sexes, age-groups, and household income. Results: Mean satisfaction with life dropped over the 16 years of study (B=-0.028, 95% CI=-0.034, -0.022), as did satisfaction with all five aspects of life. Satisfaction with school declined most rapidly (B=-0.027, 95% CI=-0.034,-0.020), becoming accelerated in the most recent 5-year window (2020-24; B=-0.139, 95% CI=-0.178,-0.099). The proportion of dissatisfied individuals rose most rapidly for schoolwork, particularly for females. Satisfaction with appearance became increasingly associated with general life satisfaction (B=0.009, 95% CI=0.005, 0.013, p<.001) and socioemotional difficulties (B=-0.051, 95% CI=-0.073,-0.029, p<.001) over time. Conclusions: Our findings add to international evidence for academic pressure and school environments as plausible drivers of recent declines in life satisfaction, particularly among female adolescents. Future studies should aim to identify the specific aspects of school life that are influencing adolescent mental health and the impact of existing educational policies on student wellbeing should be evaluated.

papers.title: Association between plasma brain-derived p-tau variants and anxiety phenotypes in older adults
papers.abstract: Objectives: To determine whether distinct anxiety phenotypes (rumination, global anxiety and worry; RAW) are associated with plasma brain-derived (BD) phosphorylated-tau (p-tau) biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease (AD) in older adults. Design: Cross-sectional observational study. Methods: Participants were 89 older adults aged 50[≥]years (mean age 64.3{+/-}8.8 years) enrolled in the RAW Brain study (R01 MH108509) in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Anxiety phenotypes were assessed using the Penn State Worry Questionnaire (PWSQ[≥]50), Rumination Subscale from the Response Style Questionnaire (RSQ>50), and Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HARS>17). Participants were classified as High-RAW if they exceeded established severity thresholds on [≥]1 domain; continuous anxiety scores were used for primary analyses. Plasma BD-tau, BD-p-tau181, BD-p-tau217, and BD-p-tau231, and matched non-BD versions were quantified using the NULISAseq CNS Panel. Associations between anxiety phenotypes and tau biomarkers were examined using multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, and APOE4 status, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. Results: Greater global anxiety was associated with higher plasma BD-p-tau181 ({beta}=0.308, 95% CI [0.003,0.048], p=0.047). This association was also observed categorically (adjusted Cohen's d=0.462, p=0.049). Worry and rumination were not associated with BD-p-tau181, and no anxiety phenotypes were associated with BD-tau, BD-p-tau217, BD-p-tau231, or corresponding non-BD alternatives. Conclusions: Greater late-life global anxiety, but not worry or rumination, was selectively associated with higher plasma BD-p-tau181. These findings extend epidemiologic evidence linking anxiety to AD risk by identifying a biologically specific blood-based correlate linking anxiety with AD-related p-tau biology. Longitudinal studies incorporating amyloid and tau biomarker confirmation are needed to determine whether anxiety precedes, accompanies, or results from early AD pathophysiology.

papers.title: Evaluation of Elicit as an adjunct search, screening, and data extraction tool for systematic reviews
papers.abstract: Background: Systematic reviews are critical for informing evidence-based medicine, policy, and future research. However, conducting a systematic review is labour- and cost-intensive and error-prone. Elicit is an AI tool that claims to replicate the systematic review process. Methods: Our study investigated Elicit's ability to replicate a systematic review by comparing its results with those of an existing systematic review recently published by our research group. We calculated accuracy, precision, sensitivity, error rate, and person-time savings at each stage of the systematic review. Results: At search, Elicit had poor overlap, finding 158 of the 5285 studies. For abstract and full-text screening, Elicit had moderate sensitivity and accuracy but poor precision, with a skew toward false positives. Elicit's data extraction tool was promising, with sentence-specific citations, and provided helpful information for 85% of values even when it did not find exact matches. Elicit offered person-time savings, taking 3.16 hours to complete the full systematic review process. Conclusions: Elicit shows promise as an adjunct screening and extraction AI tool, but in its current form, it is not ready as a standalone tool to replace the systematic review process.

papers.title: Baseline severity of positive and negative symptoms predicts relapse in opposing directions among placebo-treated schizophrenia patients: analysis of five placebo-controlled, antipsychotic withdrawal, relapse-prevention trials
papers.abstract: Background and Hypothesis Identifying which patients with schizophrenia will remain stable and which will relapse is relevant to both trial design and clinical practice. We hypothesized that higher negative and lower positive symptoms at baseline would predict longer time to relapse. Study Design This analysis pooled individual participant data on 557 patients with schizophrenia randomized to placebo from five placebo-controlled antipsychotic withdrawal relapse-prevention studies, each with a double-blind phase of at least 6 months. Relapse was defined as a [≥]12-point increase in Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) total score from double-blind baseline at any time during the double-blind phase. Cox regression analyses modeled time to relapse with the three PANSS subscales, age and sex. Study Results PANSS Negative and Positive symptom subscales predicted relapse in opposite directions and at almost equal magnitude in the pooled model. Higher negative symptoms predicted lower relapse risk (hazard ratio (HR)=0.94 per point, 95% confidence interval (CI)=0.90-0.99) and higher positive symptoms predicted higher relapse risk (HR=1.06, 95% CI=1.00-1.13). PANSS General Psychopathology did not predict relapse (HR=0.98, 95% CI=0.95-1.02). Based on the pooled estimates, a 4-point higher baseline PANSS Positive score corresponded to a 27% higher relapse risk, while a 4-point higher baseline PANSS Negative score corresponded to a 21% lower risk. Conclusions These results may help predict relapse risk in clinical care and in clinical trial samples but require prospective validation.

papers.title: Prefrontal EEG Delta-Beta Coupling Marks Depressed State in Adult Siblings
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is marked by disorganization in electrophysiological brain networks, yet it remains unclear whether such disorganization reflects the state-dependent pathological effects or a trait-like vulnerability. We analyzed resting-state electroencephalographic (EEG) delta-beta phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) in two sibling cohorts. Current-MDD families included individuals with current MDD and their currently unaffected siblings (n=36), and remitted-MDD families comprised individuals with remitted MDD and their lifetime unaffected siblings (n=110). Delta-betahigh PAC was significantly elevated (pcorr[≤]0.05) over the left-medial frontal region in participants with current MDD relative to their unaffected siblings. In the remitted-MDD families, no significant differences were observed. Regrouping all individuals irrespective of family ties into current MDD, remitted MDD, and never-depressed controls confirmed significantly elevated frontal delta-betahigh PAC at rest in the current-MDD subgroup compared to other subgroups. Overall, delta-betahigh coupling reflects the depressive state rather than a trait-like or familial vulnerability.

papers.title: Environmental predominance on brain structure and connectivity in language-related regions: a multimodal twin study in adolescence
papers.abstract: Language alterations are recognized as early markers of psychopathological vulnerability, yet genetic and environmental factors underlying language-related brain regions remain unknown. We applied univariate twin analyses and risk-discordant comparisons to multimodal dataset from 31 healthy twin pairs (9-31 years) and 17 pairs discordant for psychopathological risk (10-27 years). Gray matter volume (GMV), cortical thickness (CT), and functional interactions, specifically effective connectivity (EC), were assessed in eight bilateral language-related regions, alongside linguistic, emotional-behavioural, temperamental, and personality-related phenotypes. In healthy twin pairs (27-31 pairs, depending on data completeness), genetic and environmental determinants were estimated for all phenotypes. In 17 pairs discordant for psychopathological risk, intra-pair neuroimaging differences were tested for association with psychopathological discordance and zygosity, and individual brain measures were compared across high-risk twins, their low-risk co-twins, and healthy controls. Environmental factors predominated in structural and functional brain variability, while genetic contributions were limited, region-specific. Narrative fluency and psychological traits showed stronger heritability. Findings converged on the right middle frontal gyrus, where GMV and CT alterations reflected non-shared environment and risk expression. Despite the small sample, preliminary results suggest neurobiological vulnerability in language networks arises from environmental rather than genetic factors, informing environmental susceptibility to adolescent mental illness.

papers.title: Psychometric properties of the Alimetry Gut-Brain Wellbeing Survey-II: A revised, unidirectional mental health scale for patients with chronic gastroduodenal symptoms
papers.abstract: ObjectiveThe Alimetry Gut-Brain Wellbeing (AGBW) Survey is a validated 10-item scale developed to assess mental health in patients with chronic gastroduodenal symptoms. While the original scale demonstrated strong psychometric properties overall, as part of an ongoing commitment to continuous instrument optimization, this study evaluated a revised, unidirectional version of the scale (AGBW-II) to enhance measurement precision. MethodsThe psychometric properties of the revised AGBW-II were evaluated via an anonymous online questionnaire in a sample of 161 patients with chronic gastroduodenal symptoms. Score distributions, factor analysis, reliability, and validity were analyzed and compared with data from the validation study of the original scale (n= 311). ResultsThe AGBW-II total and subscale scores demonstrated robust reliability and validity, outperforming the original AGBW Survey. Notable improvements in the reliability and validity of the stress subscale were observed following item rewording. Confirmatory factor analysis verified the three-factor model separating the depression, stress, and anxiety subscales, with the AGBW-II showing improved model fit indices. ConclusionsThe revised, unidirectional AGBW-II demonstrated improved reliability and validity, while maintaining the underlying psychometric properties of the original scale. Consequently, the AGBW-II provides a reliable, valid, and brief mental health assessment for patients with chronic gastroduodenal symptoms.

papers.title: Differential task-related fMRI effects of a single dose of guanfacine and lisdexamfetamine in youth with ADHD: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study
papers.abstract: BackgroundStimulant and non-stimulant medications increase fronto-striato-thalamic activation in youth with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). However, comparative effects of the more recently licensed stimulant lisdexamfetamine and non-stimulant guanfacine on functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) correlates in ADHD are unknown. MethodsThis exploratory randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, crossover study compared fMRI activation in youth with ADHD during a tracking stop-signal task (SST; N = 12), a working memory task (N-back; N = 11) and a sustained attention task (SAT; N = 10), after single clinical doses of either guanfacine extended-release, lisdexamfetamine, or placebo, with one-week washouts. Twenty-one demographically matched typically developing controls (TD) were assessed once to test for potential normalisation of case-control activation differences. ResultsRegion of interest analysis showed increased right caudate and putamen activation for lisdexamfetamine versus placebo during N-back and SAT, respectively. Both drugs shared an increase in left superior temporal activation versus placebo during N-back. In whole-brain analyses only lisdexamfetamine increased precuneus/posterior cingulate activation during SST versus guanfacine, and during N-back in pre- and postcentral and occipital cortices versus placebo. During SST, placebo-treated ADHD versus TD showed reduced putamen, insula, parietal and occipital activation that was potentially attenuated/normalised under lisdexamfetamine, while under guanfacine lingual gyrus underactivation remained, with additional precuneus and middle temporal underactivation. Also, only lisdexamfetamine improved and normalised SST performance. ConclusionLisdexamfetamine appears to have stronger and drug-exclusive upregulation and potential attenuation/normalisation effects than guanfacine on basal ganglia, posterior parieto-occipital and sensorimotor activation during ADHD-relevant executive function tasks with some shared superior temporal and putamen effects. Trial registrationClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03333668; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03333668).

papers.title: Within-cohort discrimination and cross-cohort transfer of EEG-based ADHD classifiers: An exploratory two-cohort evaluation
papers.abstract: We evaluated whether participant-separated within-cohort discrimination was retained when electroencephalography (EEG) classifiers for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) were applied to a different population and recording task. This exploratory reanalysis included 121 children performing a visual task and 79 adults recorded during eyes-open rest after basic channel screening. Both cohorts used Cz/F4, 128 Hz, and the first fifteen non-overlapping 2-second epochs per participant. Fixed logistic regression and random forest classifiers used spectral, amplitude-derived, and combined features. Internal evaluation used five repetitions of five-fold participant-grouped cross-validation; bidirectional transfer fitted transformations and classifiers only on the source cohort. Adult spectral balanced accuracy (BA) was 0.9519-0.9546, compared with 0.5504-0.5664 in children. Adult spectral logistic regression exceeded all 999 internal label permutations (Monte Carlo p=0.001; within-family Holm-adjusted p=0.002). Paired spectral-minus-amplitude conditional intervals excluded zero in adults but spanned zero in children. Cross-cohort spectral BA was 0.3584-0.4675, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.0309-0.3857 in the unchanged score direction. Increasing pediatric source-epoch budgets moved random-forest AUC toward 0.5, whereas logistic-regression AUC remained below 0.1. Strong adult internal discrimination thus coexisted with reverse cross-cohort ranking. These findings characterize the evaluated pipelines, not clinical diagnostic utility or a unique mechanism: age, task, and acquisition differences were not separated, target results had previously been inspected, and conditional intervals excluded model-refitting uncertainty.

papers.title: Prospective Bidirectional Associations Between Core Schemas, Attenuated Psychotic Symptoms, and Functioning in Youth at Clinical High Risk for Psychosis
papers.abstract: ObjectiveCognitive models of psychosis implicate maladaptive core schemas in the development and emergence of psychotic symptoms, but no study has tested temporal dynamics between schemas and psychotic symptoms in a large sample of clinical high-risk (CHR) youth. Given their sizable role in cognitive behavioral therapies, the first-line treatment for CHR youth, core schemas may be key to both symptom development and treatment in this population. MethodsParticipants were 578 CHR individuals from the second North American Prodrome Longitudinal Study (NAPLS-2) assessed across five timepoints. Time-lagged mixed-effects models tested forward (schema[->]outcome) and reverse (outcome[->]schema) paths for each Brief Core Schema Scales subscale with both psychotic symptom and functioning changes, controlling for autoregressive effects, time-varying depression, and linear time. ResultsTwenty of 36 schema-outcome pairs showed significant prospective associations. Negative-other schemas were prospectively associated with worsening across nearly all psychosis symptom and functioning domains. Suspiciousness exhibited bidirectional associations with all four schema subscales. Grandiose ideas were uniquely prospectively associated with positive-self and negative-other schemas. Positive schemas were prospectively associated with decreases in suspiciousness, negative symptoms, and improvements in functioning. Effects were largely independent of depressive symptoms and robust across sensitivity analyses, with partial attenuation of self-schema effects on suspiciousness. ConclusionsCore schemas were prospectively associated with psychosis symptom and functioning change in CHR youth, with symptom-domain specificity and bidirectionality. These findings extend cognitive models of psychosis into CHR syndromes and highlight schemas as potentially modifiable treatment targets to improve outcomes in this population. papers.title: 1Hz vs. cTBS Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation to Augment Behavior Therapy for Tics: A Randomized Clinical Trial
papers.abstract: BackgroundResponse to Comprehensive Behavioral Intervention for Tics (CBIT), the first-line treatment for tic disorders, is suboptimal. We conducted Phase 1 of a two-phase, milestone-driven trial to determine if augmenting CBIT with repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to supplementary motor area (SMA) could safely engage targeted sensorimotor circuitry and improve tic controllability. MethodsIn a 3-arm, double-blind, sham-controlled randomized trial (NCT04578912), 50 youth (ages 12-21) with moderate-to-severe tics received 10 sessions of either 1Hz rTMS, continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS), or sham stimulation to the SMA, immediately followed by CBIT. Primary outcomes were safety, feasibility, and neural target engagement (fMRI SMA activation and resting-state functional connectivity [RSFC]). Secondary outcomes included change in tic controllability, tic frequency at rest, and urges. ResultsThe CBIT+TMS intervention was safe and feasible (96% completion). Treatment-related adverse events were mild-to-moderate and occurred more frequently in the 1Hz rTMS group (27% of sessions) vs. cTBS (14.7%) and sham (11.3%). While task-based SMA activation remained unchanged, cTBS demonstrated robust neural target engagement, reducing SMA-primary motor cortex (M1) RSFC and putamen-M1 RSFC. Conversely, 1Hz rTMS blunted the cortico-striatal connectivity reductions observed in the sham group. All groups exhibited significant reductions in tic frequency and improved controllability. Premonitory urges increased in the 1Hz rTMS group but decreased in sham and cTBS. ConclusionsSMA-directed cTBS is a safe, feasible augmentation that may amplify the neural effects of CBIT on sensorimotor circuitry. Findings identify cTBS as the preferred stimulation regimen for future efficacy testing. Clinical Trial RegistrationClinicalTrials.gov; Identifier: NCT04578912.

papers.title: Adolescent-Reported National Norms, Psychometrics, and Clinical Considerations for the Nationwide Quality of Life Scale (NQLS)
papers.abstract: ObjectiveThe Nationwide Quality of Life Scale (NQLS) is a brief, public-domain, youth self-report measure designed for quality of life (QoL) reporting in measurement-based care (MBC). Preliminary psychometric support comes from a sample of treatment-seeking youth, but its use in a population-based sample has not been evaluated. This study examined the NQLS psychometric performance in a U.S. nationally representative sample and develops national norms, score interpretation guidance, and clinical significance benchmarks. MethodA nationally representative sample of 1,008 youth ages 12-18 completed the NQLS as part of a larger survey battery. Analyses included exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, reliability, validity, item response theory, and generalized additive models for location, scale, and shape (GAMLSS) norming. We integrated these results with clinical data from 1,200 youth seeking treatment at a large Midwestern childrens hospital to estimate clinical significance benchmarks and compare between groups. ResultsOne- and two-factor solutions were evaluated. The NQLS demonstrated good internal consistency and convergent validity, with distinguishable "life" and "school" factors. Normative percentiles were generally stable across age, with modest narrowing at the youngest and oldest ages. Normative-sample youth showed raw score and latent trait estimates significantly higher than clinical-sample youth. ConclusionsThe NQLS provides reliable and valid measurement of QoL in a nationally representative sample. Although two structural factors were identified, the composite score is recommended for clinical decision-making. National norms and clinical significance benchmarks may facilitate MBC applications of the NQLS. Future research should evaluate its performance across additional care settings.

papers.title: Multivariate neural signatures of worry become more differentiated across adolescence and young adulthood: An ultra-high field (7T) fMRI study
papers.abstract: Worry is an important contributor to anxiety and depressive disorders, particularly in adolescence. Underlying changes in brain networks are thought to drive development of pathological worry, yet the degree to which neural correlates of worry vary by age is unknown. Here, we use multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) to investigate individual variance in brain activity during worry in a cross-sectional sample of adolescents and adults varying in worry symptoms. Participants (n=69; ages 12-31) completed a personalized worry-induction fMRI task. Brain activity was averaged across k=268 brain regions from the Shen atlas. Participants also completed self-reports assessing trait worry (PSWQ), anxiety (SCARED), and depression (MFQ) severity. A random-forest model was trained on estimated parameters from worry vs. neutral blocks using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. Age and symptomatology measures were correlated with model performance metrics. The overall cross-validated model had accuracy=66.71%, balanced accuracy=62.61%, sensitivity=80.43%, and specificity=44.78%. Trial-level accuracy increased with in-scanner worry ratings regardless of condition ({beta} =0.62, p<.001). Accuracy (r=0.30, p=.01) and balanced accuracy (r=0.31, p=.01) significantly correlated with age but did not relate to symptom severity. Brain patterns associated with worry become more differentiated across adolescence, suggesting that neural processes of worry consolidate across this period. Thus, early adolescence may be an opportune time for interventions to alter worry, but interventions adapted from adult populations may require tailoring for adolescent patients.

papers.title: Comparative Meta-Analysis of the Gut Microbiome Between ADHD and Healthy Human Cohorts
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental condition characterized by inattention, impulsivity, and hyperactivity, and is believed to involve altered dopamine signaling. Growing evidence suggests that the gut microbiome may contribute to neurobehavioral conditions, including ADHD. In this study, we examined differences in gut microbiome composition, measured using metagenomics, between healthy and ADHD-affected individuals, and evaluated age- and gender-related variation within the ADHD population. We analyzed publicly available gut microbiome datasets from the American Gut Project, NCBI, and MGnify, and retrieved data from 496 ADHD and 419 healthy individuals. Further, metadata and taxonomic abundance were processed using RStudio, normalized to sequencing depth, and analyzed at the genus level. Both groups shared several gut bacteria, including Blautia, Bacteroides, Faecalibacterium, Roseburia, and Alistipes, indicating a broadly similar core microbiome. However, individuals with ADHD showed differences in the stability and persistence of certain core taxa, such as Proteobacteria and the unclassified genus Prevotellaceae, which were uniquely present in the ADHD group. Further, PERMANOVA showed that age and gender explained a small yet significant difference in microbial variation (R2 = 0.0437, p = 0.001), with greater variability observed between males and females than across age groups. Dispersion analysis revealed significant microbial variability between males and females (p = 0.001), whereas age groups showed no significant variation (p = 0.792). Overall, these results suggest that differences in the gut microbiome between individuals with ADHD and healthy individuals are subtle. Clinically, this highlights the need to consider broader biological, environmental, and lifestyle influences-such as diet, medication use, and comorbidities-when evaluating the potential role of the gut microbiomes in ADHD. papers.title: Psychotherapy remains a human endeavor: Human therapy is valued more than AI-integrated therapy
papers.abstract: While Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into psychotherapy, little is known about how prospective patients evaluate different levels of AI involvement. Participants (n = 1,003) with depression evaluated vignettes describing psychotherapy options, from treatment delivered without AI integration (Human therapist) to treatments involving different degrees of AI integration (Assistive, Collaborative, Fully Autonomous AI). Participants consistently evaluated Human therapists more favorably, reporting a greater likelihood of seeking treatment, less hesitancy, and greater treatment acceptability. Economically, compared with a Human therapist, participants were willing to pay 31.6% less for therapists using Assistive or Collaborative AI and 57.2% less for Fully Autonomous AI. 18-19% of participants indicated that they would refuse treatment involving Assistive or Collaborative AI, compared with 31% for Fully Autonomous AI. Preference for Human over AI therapists was particularly pronounced at higher levels of therapist experience (doctoral/masters vs. peer/trainee). Overall, participants valued psychotherapy delivered by Human therapists more highly than AI integrated psychotherapy. These findings suggest that, despite increasing AI integration in mental health care, prospective patients continue to view psychotherapy as a distinctly human endeavor.

papers.title: Psychometric Properties of a 20-Item Adapted Version of the Ontario Child Health Study Emotional Behavioural Scales for Population-Based Research
papers.abstract: BackgroundThe 52-item Ontario Child Health Study Emotional Behavioural Scales (OCHS-EBS) has demonstrated reliability and validity evidence in Canadian population-based samples. This study evaluated an adapted item set of the Ontario Child Health Study Emotional Behavioural Scales (OCHS-EBS-A) intended to measure selected mental disorder symptoms while reducing respondent burden in population-based research. MethodsA prespecified candidate set of 21 items from selected OCHS-EBS disorder scales assessed depression (4 items), generalized anxiety (4 items), oppositional behaviour (6 items), and attention-deficit/hyperactivity (7 items). The 2023 Longitudinal Canadian Health Survey on Children and Youth (L-CHSCY; ages 5-21 years; n= 22,740) provided calibration and internal-validation samples. The Ontario Provincial Assessment and Tracking of Child and Family Health Study (ONPATH; Wave 5: n=719 parent and n=116 youth respondents) provided an independent sample for further evaluation. Analyses examined factorial validity, internal consistency reliability, convergent and discriminant validity, and measurement invariance across sex assigned at birth within age/informant groups. FindingsThe analyses supported a refined 20-item OCHS-EBS-A with three correlated factors representing internalizing, oppositional behaviour, and inattention/hyperactivity symptoms. Prespecified criteria for internal consistency reliability and convergent and discriminant validity were met within the reported L-CHSCY age/informant groups. Measurement invariance across sex assigned at birth was supported in the L-CHSCY groups and for children and parents in and youth-reported internalizing symptoms in ONPATH. However, not for ONPATH youth-reported oppositional behaviour symptoms. InterpretationResults from these population-based samples provide factorial-validity, internal-consistency, and convergent- and discriminant-validity evidence for scores from the 20-item OCHS-EBS-A among children, youth, and emerging adults aged 5-21 years.
